title: Active-arrow lifting fibers detect weak approximation
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the ordinary and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $f:M\to O$ be an inert-preserving map of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads with $O$ ordinary. For $C\in M$ and an active edge $\alpha:X\to f(C)$, define the lifting infinity category
$$\mathcal L_f(C,\alpha)=M_{/C}\times_{O_{/f(C)}}\{\alpha\},$$
where the pullback is a homotopy pullback of infinity categories. Thus an object is an arrow $a:D\to C$ and an equivalence from $f(a)$ to $\alpha$ in $O_{/f(C)}$; morphisms and higher simplices retain these equivalences and their coherences. Then $f$ is a weak approximation in the sense of [def-coef-operadic-weak-approximation] if and only if $\mathcal L_f(C,\alpha)$ is weakly contractible for every $C\in M$ and every active $\alpha:X\to f(C)$. No space assumption on positive-arity fibers and no categorical-fibration assumption on $f$ is imposed; the zero-fiber convention of the cited generalized-operad definition remains in force.
